findings.title: [P1] Restore interval cancellation in the polling disposer
findings.body: Calling the returned disposer no longer stops the interval. Each start/dispose cycle leaves another referenced timer running, retaining `refresh`, accumulating perpetual work, and potentially preventing Node.js processes from exiting. Preserve the timer handle and clear it during disposal.

findings.title: [P2] Remove the message listener during disposal
findings.body: The returned disposer no longer unregisters `handler`. Reusing the socket after teardown invokes stale handlers, while repeated attach/dispose cycles retain captured state and cause duplicate message processing.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup
findings.body:
After callers invoke the returned cleanup, subsequent `"message"` events still invoke the stale handler. Remounting/reconnecting accumulates handlers, causing duplicate processing and retaining obsolete state.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Clear the polling interval when cleanup is invoked
findings.body:
After callers stop polling, `refresh` continues running every second indefinitely. Repeated starts accumulate concurrent pollers, and in Node.js the live interval can also prevent process shutdown.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned teardown
findings.body:
After callers invoke the teardown, the handler remains registered. Any later `"message"` event invokes stale handlers, causing duplicate processing and retaining disposed state across reconnects or remounts.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore interval cancellation in the returned teardown
findings.body:
Invoking the returned teardown no longer stops polling. The callback continues after disposal, repeated starts accumulate timers, and in Node.js the active interval can prevent process termination.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal when detaching sockets
findings.body:
Calling the returned disposer no longer revokes the message handler. If a long-lived socket is reused after logout, tenant change, or component teardown, an untrusted peer can send later messages that still execute the stale handler under its prior session context, crossing the intended lifecycle/trust boundary.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore interval cancellation in the polling disposer
findings.body:
In Node.js, every `startPolling` call now leaves a referenced interval alive after disposal. This prevents process shutdown, retains `refresh`, and accumulates perpetual work when polling is restarted.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Remove the message listener when disposing the attachment
findings.body:
For sockets implementing `on`/`off`, invoking the returned disposer no longer releases the handler. Repeated attach/dispose cycles retain handlers and their captured state, producing duplicate message processing and unbounded listener growth.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
